sources.entry: Tiramisu - BitTorrent engine with a FUSE virtual filesystem that streams torrents live to Plex/Jellyfin without downloading (alternative to Real-Debrid). GPL-2.0 Go/Docker

summary.one_liner: Tiramisu is a Go BitTorrent engine with a FUSE virtual filesystem that presents torrent-backed .mkv, music and audiobook files as ordinary files so Plex or Jellyfin can stream them without downloading.
summary.what_it_does: The FUSE layer exposes each media file as a seekable file of the correct size, serving bytes live from a BitTorrent swarm through an in-memory pipe inside the same process. It includes a built-in sync engine that queries TMDB, searches Prowlarr (with Torrentio fallback), and files the best release, replacing it when a better one appears. Plex and Jellyfin webhooks switch a stream to priority mode on playback, and a Control Panel (:9080/control) and Health Monitor dashboard (:9080/dashboard) expose settings and live stats. A Library API and an MCP server at /mcp let HTTP clients or AI agents add and remove titles. Optional features include an SSD warmup cache, NAT-PMP port forwarding for WireGuard, and an IP blocklist. The README describes it as a single tiramisu binary.
use_cases: stream torrents to Plex without downloading
watch movies from a torrent swarm on Jellyfin
automatically build a movie and TV library from TMDB
run a streaming media server on a Raspberry Pi
file and play FLAC albums or audiobooks from torrents via Plexamp or Jellyfin
replace a Real-Debrid style debrid service
how_to_run: Run the install script from the README (Quick Install section; exact command not captured in the truncated README)
Open the Control Panel at :9080/control to set paths, TMDB key, Plex/Prowlarr credentials
Add a Plex or Jellyfin webhook pointing at http://<host>:9080/plex/webhook
Add a Samba or CIFS share of the FUSE mount as a library in Plex/Jellyfin
Trigger a sync run from the Control Panel or POST /api/scheduler/{type}/run
Build from source with: GOARCH=arm64 CGO_ENABLED=1 go build -pgo=auto -o tiramisu . (per README Step 10)
notable: FUSE filesystem and BitTorrent engine run in one process connected by an in-memory io.Pipe, with no HTTP proxy in the hot path
Adaptive Shield switches to strict verification only when corrupt pieces appear, and bans bad peers for 30 days
Built-in Go sync engine with quality ladder (4K DV down to 1080p) and automatic upgrades
Native Plex and Jellyfin webhook handling with IMDB id extraction and Priority Mode
Music and audiobook projections keyed by MusicBrainz or ASIN ids, served read-only
caveats: Initial library scan by Plex/Jellyfin opens hundreds of files and makes playback very slow until it completes, per the README's caution note
Playback depends on torrent peer availability; cold starts take 2-4 seconds per the README's measurements
Optional features (SSD warmup cache, NAT-PMP, blocklist) need extra configuration; the blocklist is off by default
